title: Material Textile Design as a Trigger for Transdisciplinary Collaboration: the Case of Coating Biobased Textiles Using Waste from Wood Industry
content: Waste production is a worldwide concern due its adverse impact on the environment, as well as on health of living beings. Sustainable development states the urgent need to implement actions to gradually replace fossil resources. This research explores the approach focused on the design of renewable materials, by developing a bio-based textile coating with the use of sawdust from radiata Pine, which is the result of industrial wood transformation processes. The methodology adopts a transdisciplinary approach, integrating knowledge from design, engineering and sociology disciplines. Perceived sawdust quality study was carried out in original format, provided by MASISA S.A. the main industry of wood panels in Chile. Two prototypes of renewable materials were developed at the Technological Center of Textile and Clothing Industry in Portugal, being evaluated from user acceptance and functional performance points of views. The mono-material design concept is explored in trade clothing design. The results obtained from users and laboratory studies favor the knife-over-roller coating and the removable clothing design, which provides improved usability performance. The conclusions highlight that transdisciplinary collaboration is essential to address complex challenges in the development of solutions, placing the design of material as a prior action in the design process of final products.
